turns.content: I'm thinking about switching from Android to iPhone. Is it worth it?

Depends what you value. iPhone wins on software polish, long-term updates, and ecosystem integration if you use a Mac or iPad. Android wins on customization, hardware variety, and often value for money.
I use a Mac laptop so maybe the ecosystem thing is relevant?

Very much so. AirDrop, Handoff, Universal Clipboard, iMessage — the integration is genuinely seamless in a way that Android-Mac combinations aren't. It adds real quality of life if you move between devices a lot.
What about the cameras? I take a lot of photos.

Both flagships are excellent. iPhone tends to produce more consistent, natural-looking results out of the camera app. Google Pixel is often considered the best computational photography on Android. Samsung prioritizes sharpening and saturation.
Will switching be a big hassle?
Less than it used to be. Apple has a Move to iOS app that handles contacts, photos, and some app data. The main friction is re-learning muscle memory and some apps behaving slightly differently.
What about all my Google apps — Gmail, Maps, Drive?
They're all on iOS and work very well. You won't lose access to any of that. Some people actually find Google apps nicer on iOS than Android.
Is the battery life on iPhones still worse than Android?
The gap has narrowed significantly with recent models. iPhone 15 Pro and beyond have strong battery life. Still, flagship Android phones with larger batteries often last longer on a charge.
What would you say is the single biggest advantage of iPhone?

Software support longevity. Apple supports iPhones for 6–7 years with OS updates. Android flagships typically get 3–4 years. If you keep phones for a long time, that's a significant practical difference.
That's actually a big deal for me. I think I'll make the switch. Thanks!
Makes sense given your setup. Take your time moving over photos and contacts before you deactivate the old device.
